newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Amcor sees lower 2nd half profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Amcor sees lower 2nd half profit.

text.p: Paper and packaging group Amcor Ltd said it expected profit for the six months ended June 30, 1997, to be lower than the year-ago period and lower than the 1996/97 first half.
Amcor also said it expected to make a significant writedown of some assets, which will be booked as abnormal items in the 1996/97 year.
In March, Amcor said in its December half results that it did not expect trading conditions to change appreciably in January/June 1997 in any of the markets in which it operated.

"This has proved to be the case in the March quarter and although Amcor has responded to margin pressure with a range of cost reduction intiatives, the savings generated have not kept pace with lower selling prices," Amcor said.

"Accordingly as there are no signs that trading conditions will change significantly in the immediate future, the company expects that profitability for the six months ended June 30, 1997 will be below the results for both January/June 1996 and July/December 1995," it said.

"In the light of continuing difficult trading conditions, directors will review the carrying value of a number of investments and operations at June 30, 1997 and expect that a number of significant write-downs of these assets will be made as abnormal items in the results for year ending June 30, 1997," Amcor said.

Amcor reported a 34.1 percent fall in net profit after abnormals of A$140.6 million for the six months ended December 31, 1996, and a 5.8 percent fall in 1995/96 net profit after abnormals of A$338.8 million.
At 2.35 p.m. (0435 GMT), Amcor shares were three cents lower at A$8.60.
